hints: Focus on what barium oxide does first when it meets water, it does not stay as an oxide.
Remember that ammonium ions release ammonia gas when warmed with a base, and barium ions give a very insoluble sulfate.
Ask yourself if anything in this mixture contains nitrogen in a form that could make brown nitrogen dioxide.
walkthrough:
**Make the base first**

Barium oxide reacts with water to form barium hydroxide, a strong soluble base.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{BaO(s) + H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{Ba(OH)}_2\text{(aq)}$$

**Release ammonia to test statement 1**

The hydroxide ions react with ammonium ions on warming to give ammonia gas and water.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{NH}_4^+\text{(aq) + OH}^-\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{NH}_3\text{(g) + H}_2\text{O(l)}$$ 
Ammonia is alkaline and turns damp red litmus blue, so statement 1 is true.

**Form the precipitate to test statement 2**

Barium ions meet sulfate ions from ammonium sulfate to form insoluble barium sulfate.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{Ba}^{2+}\text{(aq) + SO}_4^{2-}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4\text{(s)}$$ 
This is a white precipitate, so statement 2 is true.

**Check for brown gas to test statement 3**

A brown gas is $\text{NO}_2$. It forms from nitrates or nitrites on heating, not from ammonium sulfate or barium oxide.

Here only colourless $\text{NH}_3$ is evolved, so statement 3 is false. Statements 1 and 2 only are correct.

options.A: Incorrect because it claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 1 and 2 are correct but 3 is wrong as no brown $\text{NO}_2$ can form with no nitrate present.
options.B: Correct because only 1 and 2 are true. Ammonia turns damp red litmus blue and white $\text{BaSO}_4$ precipitates. No brown gas is produced.
options.C: Incorrect because it claims 2 and 3 only. Statement 2 is correct but 3 is false, and it wrongly leaves out the true statement 1 about ammonia turning litmus blue.
options.D: Incorrect because it claims only 1 is correct. Statement 1 is correct but statement 2 is also correct, the $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ and $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ precipitation cannot be ignored.
